newsitem.title: USA: US Senator considers bill delaying China MFN vote.
newsitem.headline: US Senator considers bill delaying China MFN vote.

text.p: A Republican senator is considering introducing a bill that would delay a congressional vote on renewing China's Most Favored Nation (MFN) status, a Senate aide said Tuesday.

Republican Connie Mack of Florida, who in the past has opposed MFN renewal, is considering the idea as a way to provide time to monitor China's performance as it assumes sovereignty over Hong Kong, the aide said.
President Clinton is expected to announce next month that he is renewing MFN for a further year in June. Congress will have 60 days to override that decision.
Under the idea being considered by Mack, current MFN would be extended three months meaning that Congress would vote on the year's renewal in October - well after the July 1 takeover of Hong Kong.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich has called for a six-month delay. He said he will discuss China's MFN in a foreign policy speech Wednesday.
The Senate aide said that "a lot of momentum" was building behind the idea of a three-month delay.
